claims.text: Magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons are governed by an interplay between nanoscale structural disorder and localized magnetic interactions.
Post-deposition annealing reduces nanoscale structural disorder.
Post-deposition annealing enhances localized magnetic coupling.
Reducing structural disorder improves magnetic-domain alignment.
Improved magnetic-domain alignment and stronger localized magnetic interactions enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
Improved magnetic-domain alignment and stronger localized magnetic interactions reduce hysteresis during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will exhibit a greater magnetocaloric response than the as-deposited baseline under low applied fields.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline under low applied fields.
Heat-transfer rates constrain the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Nanoscale dimensions may limit the improvement in magnetocaloric response and hysteresis obtained by annealing.
Heat-transfer constraints may limit the observed improvement in magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
The proposed test compares an as-deposited set with a controlled-annealing set under low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.

Failure of the annealed samples to show either a statistically significant magnetocaloric-response increase or a hysteresis reduction relative to the as-deposited samples is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
